claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into both operands of every SqlBinaryExpression, including AndAlso and OrElse, which do not propagate NULL under three-valued logic, so the IS NOT NULL test is wrongly dropped. The file's own ProcessNullNotNull guard at line 2313 excludes exactly those operators; without it, queries like g.LeaderNickname != null ? g.LeaderNickname.Length > 3 || g.HasSoulPatch : null start matching rows where LeaderNickname IS NULL.
raw: #1 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AndAlso`/`OrElse` as NULL-propagating, contradicting the file's own rule and changing query results

claim: The guard does not distinguish a scalar result from a search-condition result, so the optimization fires on boolean results. SqlNullabilityProcessor runs before SQL Server's SearchConditionConvertingExpressionVisitor, whose ConvertToValue emits CASE WHEN c THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, so once the enclosing ELSE NULL is removed a NULL condition silently becomes false (e.g. x.NullableIntA != null ? (bool?)(x.NullableIntA > 5) : null returns false instead of null).
raw: #2 High: dropping the `ELSE NULL` destroys the NULL of a boolean when-clause result on SQL Server (`null` becomes `false`)

claim: All five added tests project scalar results through genuinely NULL-propagating operators; nothing projects a boolean result and nothing routes the null-checked operand through AndAlso/OrElse, so both unsound shapes are uncovered and the suite passes with the defects present. Several new branches (ExpressionType.Negate, the right-side drop arm, the binary.Update arm, InstancePropagatesNullability) are also unexercised.
raw: #3 Medium: the new tests exercise only the always-safe shapes; both defect classes above are uncovered

claim: RestoreNullValueColumnsList(currentNonNullableColumnsCount) passes the non-nullable-columns counter to the null-value list restore, whereas line 529 correctly uses currentNullValueColumnsCount. _nullValueColumns is therefore truncated to the wrong length, either losing valid IS NULL knowledge or leaking stale entries into a later when-clause or the ELSE. Pre-existing since 17a9035ad (2023-10-23).

claim: Removing the CASE guard means clause.Result is now evaluated for rows the guard excluded, which could surface runtime errors (divide-by-zero, conversion overflow) that the CASE suppressed. No case could be constructed where a NULL operand triggers an error rather than yielding NULL, and SQL Server does not guarantee CASE short-circuiting anyway. Marked [unverified].
